summary: Runner re-auth window causes Maven artifact publish failures during KMS/Vault secret rotation
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled Vault rewrap and KMS key rotation in prod us-east, a subset of self-hosted CI runners failed to refresh their auth session within the re-auth grace window. Long-running Maven publish jobs (gradle/maven artifacts) observed 401/403 from the artifact registry and the CI controller marked runners as disconnected, leading to queued/pending deploys across several release pipelines.

Impact:
- ~120 CI jobs stalled across nightly release and customer-facing release branches for ~45 minutes.
- Artifact publish failures impacted two Canary releases (canary-frontend v1.12.7 and canary-runtime v3.4.0).
- No data loss; artifacts not published and must be requeued or republished.

Environment:
- prod us-east (k8s cluster: ci-runner-prod-01)
- Runner type: ephemeral self-hosted (ephemeral-runner-controller v2.8.1)
- Vault: transit rewrap triggered (vault-cluster-prod, transit rekey job)
- Artifact Registry: internal-nexus (https://nexus.internal.redwood)

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Trigger Transit rewrap / KMS rotation for Vault (same procedure as scheduled maintenance).
2) Observe ephemeral runners performing token refresh at next heartbeat window.
3) If runner's token-refresh overlaps with Vault rewrap and KMS latency spike, runner fails to exchange token and marks itself Unregistered for >30s.
4) Long-running build that tries to push artifacts during this window receives 401/403 and fails stage.

Observed logs / errors (representative):
- runner pod logs: "ERROR auth: token refresh failed: transit/rewrap: decryption failed"
- ephemeral-runner-controller: "WARN runner-heartbeat: missed-heartbeat: marking runner unavailable (grace window exceeded)"
- maven publish step: "Failed to deploy artifacts: Server returned HTTP response code: 401 for URL: https://nexus.internal.redwood/..."
- controller events: "PodNotReady -> JobRetryScheduled"

Initial investigation notes:
- Vault transit rewrap produced a short period (~20–60s) of elevated API latency in us-east. KMS key re-encryption added to the latency.
- Runner token refresh logic has a strict re-auth grace window of 30s before CI controller evicts. Many runners retried immediately with no jitter, causing thundering refresh retries against Vault.
- Artifact publish failures correlate 1:1 with runner eviction events (publish attempted from ephemeral runner that lost token mid-upload).
- There is no bug in Nexus; requests that include a valid fresh token succeed.

Temporary mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2026-03-09 02:18 UTC: CS and SRE paused non-critical nightly releases and set affected pipelines to manual re-run.
- 2026-03-09 02:28 UTC: Increased runner-controller grace window from 30s -> 120s (hotfix flag enabled) to reduce eviction during in-flight token refresh.
- 2026-03-09 02:35 UTC: Applied client-side retry/backoff to maven publisher step via pipeline wrapper script (retry 3x with exponential backoff).
- 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC: Requeued failed publish jobs; most completed successfully after re-run.

Root-cause hypothesis:
- Combination of KMS-backed Vault transit rewrap latency spike and aggressive runner re-auth eviction policy. Lack of jitter on token refresh amplified load on Vault causing some refreshes to fail temporarily.

Permanent remediation proposals:
1) Add randomized jitter and exponential backoff to runner token refresh to avoid thundering herd during Vault operations.
2) Make runner-controller re-auth grace configurable per deployment and set safer default (e.g., 90–120s) for prod.
3) Add limited buffering/stream-resume support for artifact uploads so mid-upload auth refresh does not force failure (longer-term engineering task).
4) Update Vault rewrap runbook to include a temporary throttle on agent refresh endpoints and coordinate with CI to drain long-running publish jobs before rewrap.

Follow-ups / Owners:
- Engineering: implement jitter + backoff on runner agent (owner: @marcus-patel) — linked ticket INT-942321.
- Platform: change default grace window and expose operator flag (owner: @sre-oncall) — linked ticket INT-942322.
- Release Engineering: add pre-rotation drain step for artifact pushes (owner: @olivia-chen) — linked ticket INT-942323.

Links and artifacts:
- Slack: #infra-ci thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0ICRI0/thread-xyz
- GitHub (temporary pipeline wrapper PR): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-config/pull/814
- Runbook draft for Vault rewrap: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=1284921
